title: Launch Gateway Tempo and Capacity Sentinel
creator: Maya Singh
description: Goal: Create a coordinated cadence (Gateway Tempo) and an automated Capacity Sentinel that governs reserved capacity allocations, launch hold/safe-mode triggers, and upfront communication signals across Runtime, Console, and API surfaces. Background: multiple launches in the last two quarters created contention on dedicated pools and ambiguous cutover signals. This initiative defines signal thresholds, ownership handoffs, and lightweight automation to reduce manual coordination during busy release windows.
acceptance_criteria: A shared weekly launch cadence is documented and adopted by runtime/console/api teams, with a single canonical Slack channel and calendar source of truth.
Capacity Sentinel runs as a scheduled job and flags any launch request where committed reserved capacity would exceed 80% of pool availability or would leave headroom under 20% for burst lanes.
Automatic pre-flight email/Slack notifications are sent to stakeholders when a launch request crosses thresholds; a single-click hold is available in the Console launch UI.
Canary policy defined: per-region rolling canary windows and automated rollback escalation matrix included in runbook.
Post-launch telemetry dashboard shows per-launch token cost delta, peak qps, and SLO breaches with linkable drilldowns for postmortems.
acceptance_test_plan: Simulate three concurrent launch requests that would together consume 85% of a dedicated pool and verify Capacity Sentinel blocks the third and posts a hold note.
Validate Slack/email preflight notifications include clear next actions and links to the Console hold button and capacity dashboard.
Run a controlled canary rollback by toggling the single-click hold and verify automated rollback notifications and incident creation in PagerDuty.
Verify post-launch dashboard populates within 10 minutes of cutover and includes token-cost/time series and latency percentiles.
